books.name: Archivus's Riddles
books.focus: Hardly had… · But for… · no option but to · reputed to

items.a: The knights fled the moment the dragon appeared.
items.tip: Hardly had + subject + past participle + when… = as soon as (formal inversion).
items.say: Hardly had the dragon appeared when the knights fled.

items.a: The new rules had no effect on how long we could play.
items.b: The new rules ___ to how long we could play.
items.tip: make no difference to = have no effect on.
items.say: The new rules made no difference to how long we could play.

items.a: She was not at all surprised by the news.
items.tip: not in the least = not at all.
items.say: She was not in the least surprised by the news.

items.a: Ollie only finished the race because his friends cheered him on.
items.b: But ___ cheering him on, Ollie would never have finished the race.
items.tip: But for + noun = if it hadn't been for…
items.say: But for his friends cheering him on, Ollie would never have finished the race.

items.a: It is said that the castle has a hidden room.
items.tip: be reputed to + verb = people say that…
items.say: The castle is reputed to have a hidden room.

items.a: Joe is extremely unlikely to win the quiz.
items.b: There is ___ Joe will win the quiz.
items.tip: extremely unlikely = there is little chance that…
items.say: There is little chance that Joe will win the quiz.

items.a: The explorers had to turn back because of the storm.
items.b: The storm left the explorers ___ turn back.
items.tip: leave someone (with) no option but to = force them to.
items.say: The storm left the explorers with no option but to turn back.

items.a: I didn't mean to upset Ava.
items.tip: have no intention of + -ing = not mean to.
items.say: I had no intention of upsetting Ava.

books.name: Shades of Meaning
books.focus: like a duck to water · spill the beans · in the balance

items.a: Rosa learned to juggle very quickly and naturally.
items.tip: take to something like a duck to water = learn it easily and naturally.
items.say: Rosa took to juggling like a duck to water.

items.a: Tom told everyone the secret by accident.
items.tip: spill the beans = tell a secret.
items.say: Tom accidentally spilled the beans.

items.a: The result of the match was very uncertain until the end.
items.b: The result of the match ___ until the end.
items.tip: hang in the balance = be very uncertain.
items.say: The result of the match hung in the balance until the end.

items.a: Please don't tell anyone about the surprise party.
items.b: Please don't ___ about the surprise party.
items.tip: not breathe a word = not tell anyone at all.
items.say: Please don't breathe a word to anyone about the surprise party.

items.a: Mia is still learning how to play chess, so be patient.
items.b: Mia hasn't ___ chess yet, so be patient.
items.tip: get the hang of something = learn how to do it.
items.say: Mia hasn't got the hang of chess yet, so be patient.

items.a: It was obvious that Kai was nervous.
items.tip: There's no doubt / no denying that… = it is clear that…
items.say: There was no doubt that Kai was nervous.

items.a: The magician's trick completely amazed the audience.
items.tip: take someone's breath away = amaze them.
items.say: The magician's trick took the audience's breath away.

items.a: Stop worrying so much about the quiz; it's not important.
ans: making a mountain out of a molehill
items.tip: make a mountain out of a molehill = treat a small problem as a big one.
items.say: Stop making a mountain out of a molehill — it's only a quiz!

books.name: Grand Wordcraft
books.focus: insisted that we arrive · Try as he might · Should you…

items.a: 'You must all arrive on time,' the teacher told us.
items.tip: insist that + subject + base verb (the subjunctive) or insist on + -ing.
items.say: The teacher insisted that we arrive on time.

items.a: Zara had no idea at all how to solve the puzzle.
items.b: Zara hadn't ___ how to solve the puzzle.
items.tip: not have the slightest idea = have no idea at all.
items.say: Zara hadn't the slightest idea how to solve the puzzle.

items.a: However hard he tried, Ben couldn't open the jar.
items.tip: Try as he might = however hard he tried (literary).
items.say: Try as he might, Ben couldn't open the jar.

items.a: People don't appreciate how much bees do for us.
items.b: Bees ___ for how much they do for us.
ans: aren't given the credit they deserve
items.tip: give someone credit for = recognise what they have done.
items.say: Bees are not given enough credit for how much they do for us.

items.a: If you need help, press the star button.
items.tip: Should + subject + verb = if (formal conditional inversion).
items.say: Should you need help, press the star button.

items.a: The team's success depends completely on how well they work together.
items.b: The team's success ___ how well they work together.
items.tip: hinge on = depend completely on.
items.say: The team's success hinges entirely on how well they work together.

items.a: Only when the storm stopped did we leave the cave.
ans: did not leave the cave until
items.tip: Only when… did we… = We didn't … until…
items.say: We did not leave the cave until the storm had stopped.

items.a: Ellie's idea was so clever that everyone was amazed.
ans: Such was the cleverness of Ellie's idea
Such was the brilliance of Ellie's idea
items.tip: Such was + noun + that… is a formal way to stress how great something was.
items.say: Such was the cleverness of Ellie's idea that everyone was amazed.
